title: Continuity/epoch state must be explicit
requirement: Where a Clank derives novelty, alerting, or editorial state from comparison against its own prior local history, a discontinuity in that history (data loss, restore from an older backup, a re-baseline, a collector/source replacement that breaks continuity, a region change that invalidates prior comparisons) MUST be represented as an explicit, queryable fact about the dataset's timeline — distinct both from the records themselves and from any novelty judgement made using those records. Baseline/bootstrap observations (the first population of a source or a re-population after a continuity break) MUST be distinguishable, at read time, from ordinary ongoing observations made after continuity was established. A Clank MUST NOT allow historical or baseline-era records to silently acquire the semantics of current, continuously-observed records merely because they are present in the same table as current records.
trigger: Applies to any Clank that derives novelty, alerting, or editorial freshness judgements from comparison against its own prior local history (i.e., a persistent Clank with a concept of 'seen before'). Does not apply to a Clank with no such comparison logic — a purely stateless collector, or one that never derives novelty from local history, has nothing for this standard to bind.
rationale: Evidenced by four independent implementations (watch-clank's OperationalEpoch, oem-radar's documented cutover procedure, feature-phone-clank's and smartwatch-clank's continuity.py) and a near-complete, currently-PROPOSED clank-architecture draft (ADR-0006) that smartwatch-clank already builds against. A real, dated incident (watch-clank's Timex catalogue backfill burst) demonstrates the failure mode directly: baseline-era records re-alerted as fresh after a restore/backfill because continuity state was not explicit enough for the alerting logic to distinguish them. Absence of this distinction is not a hypothetical risk — it has already produced a large false-novelty burst in production. This standard adopts the substance of ADR-0006's continuity concept (an explicit continuity/epoch fact, baseline distinguishability, 'a fresh baseline is never novelty') as the Pass 1 starting contract for Standards Clank, without copying its exact schema — see notes for what was adopted vs. left open.
forbidden: Treating a fresh bootstrap/re-baseline as ordinary novelty or current-state continuity because no explicit signal exists to say otherwise
Relying solely on operator memory, a manually-invoked CLI flag, or an undocumented convention to mark a continuity break, where that reliance leaves no durable, queryable trace in the dataset itself
A downstream novelty/alerting consumer having no way to determine whether a given record predates the current continuity epoch
acceptance: The dataset carries an explicit, queryable representation of continuity boundaries (an epoch marker, a gap record, a baseline flag on the affected records, or an equivalent mechanism) — the specific mechanism is not prescribed
Baseline/bootstrap observations are distinguishable from ordinary post-continuity observations by a downstream reader, without needing out-of-band knowledge
After a data-loss/restore/re-baseline/collector-replacement/region-change event that breaks continuity, the discontinuity itself is recorded as durably as the records on either side of it
A downstream consumer deriving novelty or alerting from local history can determine, for any given record, whether it falls inside a recognized continuity gap or baseline window

evidence.summary: A never-baselined local database produced a ~1045-event burst; the addendum documents that production's own operational_epochs table is empty, with baseline protection resting entirely on a manually-passed flag.

A near-complete draft ContinuityEvent contract (DATA_LOSS/RESTORE_FROM_BACKUP/NEW_BASELINE/EPOCH_BOUNDARY/OBSERVATION_GAP/SCHEDULER_OUTAGE/UNKNOWN_CONTINUITY); 'a fresh baseline is never novelty'; 'absence is never zero'. smartwatch-clank explicitly builds against this ADR.

evidence.source: watch-clank OperationalEpoch model; oem-radar documented Epoch-1/Epoch-2 cutover procedure; feature-phone-clank and smartwatch-clank core/continuity.py
evidence.summary: Four independent implementations of the same underlying concept, three with no cross-citation to each other or to ADR-0006.

notes: Pass 1 draft (docs/data-ontology/pass1/dossier-c1-continuity-explicitness.md), from Pass 0B adjudication candidate C1 (docs/data-ontology/pass0/candidates/c1-continuity-explicitness.md), from Pass 0A cluster baseline-epoch-continuity (docs/data-ontology/pass0/clusters/baseline-epoch-continuity.md). Adopted from ADR-0006: the concept of an explicit, queryable continuity fact distinct from ordinary records, and the 'fresh baseline is never novelty' principle. Deliberately NOT adopted from ADR-0006: its specific ContinuityEvent type enum and any particular storage shape — this standard does not mandate an operational_epochs table, a specific event-type vocabulary, or any other implementation detail; ADR-0006 remains clank-architecture's own PROPOSED document, cited as evidence, not incorporated by reference. RATIFIED 2026-08-31 by operator ruling, Pass 2 approved unmodified, Pass 3 ratification survey recommended RATIFY AS WRITTEN, decision record decisions/0010-data-com-001-decision.md. watch-clank's empty-production-epoch-table exposure remains a pre-existing, separately-flagged operator risk, not evidence of a violation of this now-ratified standard — any specific-Clank conformance finding requires a normal audit. korean-tech-wire's resulting remediation-backlog item is an expected, not assumed, consequence of ratification.
